The dev server is live, and the repo's own demo script (`web/src/lib/demo.ts`) documents the canonical fix and the `'theme'` storage key. The bug is clear:

- `useState(false)` at `App.tsx:22` — the theme always starts light, ignoring any prior choice
- the effect at `App.tsx:32-34` applies the theme to the DOM but never writes it anywhere durable

Applying the minimal fix — read the initial value from `localStorage`, and write back on every change:

content.text:
Kane is green — the full flow (toggle on → hard reload → background still dark) passes in a real browser against the live app.

The fix, both lines in `target-app/src/App.tsx`:

```
- const [isDark, setIsDark] = useState(false)
+ const [isDark, setIsDark] = useState(() => localStorage.getItem('theme') === 'dark')

  useEffect(() => {
    document.body.dataset.theme = isDark ? 'dark' : 'light'
+   localStorage.setItem('theme', isDark ? 'dark' : 'light')
  }, [isDark])
```

The theme had only ever lived in React state, so every reload reset it to `false`. Now the initial state reads the persisted choice (lazy initializer, so `localStorage` is read once on mount rather than on every render), and the existing effect that applies the theme to `document.body` also writes it back — keeping the DOM and storage in sync from a single place, including the initial mount.

Two notes on what I did and didn't touch:

- I left `index.html` alone, per the working agreement to edit only `./src`. The tradeoff is a one-frame light flash on reload before React mounts and the effect runs — Kane's assertion passes regardless, but if you want that flash gone, the standard fix is a small inline script in `index.html` that sets `document.body.dataset.theme` from `localStorage` before the bundle loads. Say the word and I'll add it.
- I used the key `'theme'` to match the convention already documented in `web/src/lib/demo.ts`.
